page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What lymph is
steps.why: Lymph is blood plasma that has already left the capillaries, so saying where it comes from explains everything that is missing from it.
common_mistakes: Calling lymph a part of blood. It flows in its own vessels, not in the blood vessels.
Writing that it is red. Lymph is colourless.
steps.memory_tip: Lymph is the fluid that leaked out of the blood and is on its way back.
steps.margin_note: Where it is and where it comes from. Two or three lines.
lines: Lymph is the colourless interstitial fluid that
It is formed from the fluid that leaves the
blood capillaries into the tissue spaces.

steps.label: How it differs from plasma
steps.why: Only small molecules cross the capillary wall, so the cells and the large proteins stay behind in the blood, and that is the whole difference.
common_mistakes: Writing that lymph has no cells at all. It carries lymphocytes.
Saying lymph and plasma are the same. Lymph lacks the red cells, platelets and large proteins.
steps.memory_tip: Whatever is too big to cross the capillary wall stays in the plasma: red cells, platelets, large proteins.
steps.margin_note: Three things missing and one thing present. Boxing the list makes it quick to read.

lines.text: No red cells, no platelets, few big proteins

lines: Lymph has no red blood cells and no platelets.
It carries much less protein than plasma,
because the large plasma proteins cannot pass
Lymphocytes are the cells it does carry.

insider_note: The three missing items are the marked list — red blood cells, platelets and large plasma proteins — and lymphocytes are the one thing that must NOT be missing.
